title: ADS129x low-power 8-channel 24-bit analog front-end datasheet SBAS459K (ADS1294/ADS1296/ADS1298)
what_they_did: The ADS1298 datasheet gives the RLD amplifier feedback network as 1 MΩ in parallel with 1.5 nF (typical values) and states that stabilizing the entire RLD loop is specific to the individual system; it also recommends a nonferroelectric tantalum or C0G/NPO capacitor on VCAP1 in vibration and documents CLKSEL, CLK_EN and START.
useful_for_us: It is the primary source for Q1-Q4: it disproves the 392 kΩ || 10 nF premise, gives the real 1 MΩ || 1.5 nF values, the internal-versus-external RLDREF rule, the exact VCAP1 piezoelectric warning, and the master-clock and START synchronisation rules.

title: Improving common-mode rejection using the right-leg drive amplifier (TI application report SBAA188)
what_they_did: This TI application report analyses the closed-loop RLD system and says stability is the major concern because the protection resistor and cable impedance form a low-pass pole that can be as low as 2 kHz; it adds a zero with CP and sets bandwidth with CF, and its measured board uses 670 kΩ with 1.8 nF while its comparison table uses 1 MΩ || 1.5 nF.
useful_for_us: It is the closest published stability analysis for Q1 and explains why a high contact resistance and a series protection resistor threaten the RLD loop, while giving concrete TI component values other than 392 kΩ || 10 nF.

title: ADS1298: RLD feedback/filter (TI E2E thread 780513) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A TI employee answers a question about the RLD feedback/feedthrough path and says that adding a low-pass filter there would be detrimental to properly closing the RLD loop, and that the datasheet's word filter should have been series resistance or feedthrough.
useful_for_us: It shows that TI distinguishes the RLD feedback network from a low-pass filter in the RLDOUT-to-RLDIN path, which matters when reading the 392 kΩ || 10 nF assumption in Q1.

title: ADS1298: RLD circuit simulation (TI E2E thread 880544) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A TI employee tells a designer asking for an RLD design procedure to start with the 1 MΩ || 1.5 nF feedback circuit used in the RLD application note, and says TI has no separate step-by-step procedure because it has no public verified models of the internal amplifiers.
useful_for_us: It is the direct TI recommendation for Q1: use 1 MΩ || 1.5 nF as the starting point, not 392 kΩ || 10 nF, and do not expect a TI-verified stability model.

title: ADS1298: RLD output circuit (TI E2E thread 909467) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A TI employee says the RLD electrode should get protection similar to the other electrode inputs, that the internal RLD amplifier short-circuit current is only about plus or minus 250 microamps, and that the 100 kΩ resistor shown in the datasheet is merely an example.
useful_for_us: It confirms that the series resistor at RLDOUT is a free design choice rather than a fixed datasheet value, which is relevant to the 10 kΩ series resistor in Q1.

title: ADS1298: How to design clock circuits for synchronous sampling of two ADS1298? (TI E2E thread 1684949) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A TI employee answers that an external clock can be shared with the CLK pin of both devices with CLKSEL set to 0 on each, or that the primary device can output its internal oscillator to the second device, and refers to the datasheet multiple-device section.
useful_for_us: It answers the clock-sharing topology in Q4 but gives no series resistor, buffer, cable-length or clock-noise guidance, which is exactly the remaining gap.

title: ADS1298: VCAP1 and WCT capacitor values (TI E2E thread 1634560) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A TI employee confirms that 100 pF on WCT is fine and that 22 microfarads on VCAP1 is recommended for the ADS1294/ADS1298, while 100 microfarads is recommended only on the lower-noise ADS1299; the thread discusses capacitance values and not capacitor dielectric.
useful_for_us: It confirms the 22 microfarad VCAP1 value for Q3, leaving the dielectric and microphonics answer to the datasheet's power-supply section.

title: How to change RLDREF for ADS1298 (TI E2E thread 207287) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: Two TI employees explain that the RLDREF pin can be driven internally from Vdd/2 or the WCT node, or by the user's own external source, and that the evaluation board provides resistor and trim-pot pads for an adjustable external reference.
useful_for_us: It confirms that the external divider option in Q2 is a supported configuration, but it reports no noise comparison against the internal reference.

title: ADS1298: Noise on the ECG signals, internal RLD amp is used (TI E2E thread 1278584) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A TI employee's noise-troubleshooting checklist tells the designer to try the internal RLD amplifier first by setting RLDREF_INT=1 to use the internal mid-supply voltage, then to disable extra features and check one channel at a time.
useful_for_us: It shows TI's practical preference for the internal RLDREF when debugging noise in Q2, while still giving no measured internal-versus-external noise difference.

title: NINA-B3 series stand-alone Bluetooth LE modules data sheet UBX-17052099 R15
what_they_did: The NINA-B3 data sheet marks specific module pins as radio sensitive, states that digital noise on pins close to the radio part of the RF chip can reduce radio sensitivity, and gives a footnote recommending frequencies below 10 kHz and standard drive strength on those pins; its pin table also says VBUS must be connected to 5 V for the USB interface to work.
useful_for_us: It supplies the exact Q6 wording, the complete radio-sensitive pin list and the 10 kHz limit, and it is the NINA-B306-specific Q5 statement about VBUS.

title: NINA-B3 series system integration manual UBX-17056748 R15
what_they_did: The NINA-B3 system integration manual gives the antenna placement rules for the NINA-B3x6 PCB-trace antenna, including that a large ground plane is a prerequisite and that the plane should extend at least 10 mm on both sides of the module, and it warns not to place components close to the antenna area.
useful_for_us: It provides the official 10 mm ground-plane recommendation and the 5 mm or 10 mm casing clearance rules needed to judge the Q6 question about a small ground plane beside the antenna.

title: nRF52840 Product Specification v1.1 (full text mirror of Nordic document 4413_417 v1.1)
what_they_did: The nRF52840 Product Specification says in section 5.3.2 that when using the USB peripheral a 5 V USB supply needs to be provided on the VBUS pin, lists VBUS in the USB operating conditions, and its reference-circuit tables include configurations with USB disabled; the text does not contain an explicit rule for VBUS when USB is never used.
useful_for_us: It is the primary Nordic document for Q5 and shows that the official wording is conditional, which is why the definitive tie-to-GND instruction has to come from the reference design and the Nordic forum.

title: nRF52840 Unused USB bus (Nordic DevZone thread 35658) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A DevZone reply about an unused nRF52840 USB interface says D+ and D- can be left unconnected and VBUS connected to GND, and points to circuit configuration number 6 in the nRF52840 Product Specification reference circuitry, which is the configuration with USB disabled.
useful_for_us: It gives the direct Q5 answer, tie VBUS to GND, and links it to the official non-USB reference configuration rather than leaving it as an unsupported forum opinion.

title: Pin configurations for GPIO pins on NINA-B306-00B nRF52840 BLE module (Nordic DevZone thread 116718) (read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A designer asks whether a set of NINA-B306 GPIO assignments for SPI, I2C and ADC will work, explains that the chosen pins are not radio sensitive so the 10 kHz limit does not apply, and a community reply says all nRF52840 interfaces can be assigned to any pin as long as no high-frequency clock is placed on a low-frequency-only pin.
useful_for_us: It is the closest public discussion of putting an I2C bus on or near the NINA-B306 radio-sensitive pins, and it shows the community treats the 10 kHz footnote as a hard constraint rather than a suggestion.

title: ADS1x9xECG-FE user's guide (TI SLAU384A)
what_they_did: The ADS1x9xECG-FE user's guide documents the evaluation board schematic and bill of materials, including its RLD network, where the series part R35 is a 100 kΩ resistor and no 392 kΩ feedback resistor appears in the RLD example.
useful_for_us: It rules out the TI evaluation board as the origin of the 392 kΩ || 10 nF value and shows that the series resistor at the RLD output is a board-level choice rather than a fixed datasheet value.

title: What do you do with the USB pins if you are not using USB? (Nordic DevZone thread 48589, read through the public r.jina.ai text proxy because the site returns 403 to direct fetches)
what_they_did: A DevZone reply says you have to ground VBUS when the nRF52840 USB peripheral is not used, that D- and D+ can be left floating or grounded, and that these USB-only pins cannot be used as GPIOs.
useful_for_us: It independently repeats the Q5 instruction to tie VBUS to GND and adds the warning that the USB pins are not general-purpose I/O, so the answer does not depend on a single forum post.

title: ADS1299: Right leg drive closed loop bandwidth — RC in datasheet and EK (TI E2E thread 400935)
what_they_did: The thread compares the datasheet and SBAA188 RLD network (1 MΩ || 1.5 nF) with the 392 kΩ || 10 nF used on the ADS1299EEG-FE board; the TI reply agrees that the board's ≈40 Hz bandwidth is too low to reject 50/60 Hz common mode and says the origin of the EVM values is unknown.
useful_for_us: It is the only page found that uses the 392 kΩ || 10 nF value, so it identifies where the question's premise comes from and records TI's own view that the EVM network should not be copied.

title: VUSB connection to GND, if USB will not be used (Nordic DevZone thread 69598)
what_they_did: The asker quotes the nRF52833 reference circuitry as connecting VBUS and DECUSB directly to GND when USB is unused, and the Nordic employee's answer recommends keeping the C18/C19 footprints and fitting a 0 Ω resistor instead of C18 if USB turns out unused.
useful_for_us: It confirms that the non-USB reference configuration ties VBUS to GND, but the answer itself is about the capacitors, so it supports rather than replaces the nRF52840 Product Specification wording.

title: Is it normal for a NINA-B306 module to have an extremely short range? (u-blox portal thread)
what_they_did: The page returned only the u-blox Portal client-side loading shell; the question body, answers and date are rendered by JavaScript and were not readable, so no content from it is claimed.
useful_for_us: It shows the thread with this exact title exists (matching the Q6 range sub-question) but cannot be cited, which is why that part stays OPEN.

title: PCB size required for NINA-B302 vs B306 (u-blox portal thread)
what_they_did: The page returned only the u-blox Portal client-side loading shell; no question, answer or date text was readable, so nothing from this thread is quoted.
useful_for_us: It confirms that a thread about PCB size and the NINA-B306/B302 comparison exists, but it does not answer the small-ground-plane question, so Q6 stays OPEN on that point.
